content.text: In one or two sentences, explain what Rust programming language is and why memory safety matters.

We need to explain Rust and why memory safety matters in one or two sentences. Keep concise. Rust is a systems programming language that focuses on safety, speed, and concurrency, using a borrow checker to enforce memory safety without garbage collection. Memory safety matters because it prevents common bugs like buffer overflows and use-after-free, which can lead to crashes, security vulnerabilities, and undefined behavior.

choice.text: Rust is a systems programming language that ensures memory safety at compile time through its ownership model and borrow checker, eliminating common bugs without needing a garbage collector. Memory safety is crucial because it prevents vulnerabilities like buffer overflows and dangling pointers, which can cause crashes, data corruption, or security exploits.
